representing first informant.
2. Perused the record.

3. Instant bail application has been filed by applicant-Abhishek Kumar seeking his enlargement on bail in Case Crime No. 191 of 2023 under Sections 498A, 304B I.P.C. and Sections 3/4 D. P. Act Police Station-Kiratpur, District- Bijnor during the pendency of trial.

sentences.text: It transpires from record that in respect of an incident which is alleged to have occurred on 02.05.2023, a delayed F.I.R. dated 03.05.2023 was lodged by first informant Munesh Singh (father of the deceased), which was registered as Case Crime No. 0191 of 2023 under Sections 498A, 304B I.P.C. and Sections 3/4 D. P. Act Police Station-Kiratpur, District- Bijnor.
In the aforesaid F.I.R. five persons namelyNitin, Abhishek, Shymo Devi and Rajesh have been nominated as named accused.
5. Record Shows that marriage of Nitin, brother of applicant, was solemnized with Saloni fiver years prior of the F.IR.

However. just after expiry of a period of five years from the date of marriage of brother of applicant an unfortunate incident occurred on 02.05.2023 in which bhabhi of the applicant consumed some poisonous substance.
It is the case of applicant that she was immediately rushed to the hospital but she was declared brought dead by the Doctor.

6. Learned counsel for applicant contends that thought the applicant is a named and charge-sheeted accused inasmuch as the charge-sheet has been submitted against applicant on 28.06.2023 yet he is liable to be enlarged on bail.
Applicant is the devar of the deceased.
With reference to the Site Plan prepared by the Investigating Officer, copy of which is on record at page 54 of the paper book, he submits that applicant was living separately.
Apart from above, applicant cannot be said to be the beneficiary of the alleged additional demand of dowry.

7. It is next contended that by the learned counsel for applicant co-accused Smt. Ramo @ Ramrati and Rajesh, who are mother-in-law and father-in-law of deceased have already been enlarged on bail by this Court vide order dated 07.07.2023 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 29254 of 2023 (Smt. Ramo Alias Ramrati and another Vs. State of U.P.).

sentences.text:
For ready reference, the order dated 07.07.2023 is extracted herein under:-
"

By means of the the bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.191 of 2023 at Police Station-Kiratpur, District-Bijnor under Sections 498A, 304B I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.?
The applicant is in jail since 08.05.2023.
The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 06.06.2023.

The following arguments made by Shri Bhuvnesh Kumar Singh, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Shrawan Kumar Dubey, learned AGA from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1. The applicants are the mother-in-law and father-in-law of the deceased respectively.
2. The applicants did not torture the deceased nor did they demand dowry.
3. They never interfered in the marital life of the deceased and her husband.
The applicants are bereaved by the death of their daughter-in-law.

sentences.text: 4. However, for the purpose of this bail application it is submitted that the deceased was a temperamental lady who was prone to extreme reactions even over trivial issues.
5. On the fateful day, over some minor disagreements with her members of the households, the victim took some poisonous substance in a fit of rage without knowledge of the applicants.
When the deceased started showing signs of physical discomfort, the husband of the deceased promptly rushed her to the hospital.
The victim died in hospital while she was under treatment.
6. The applicants did not aid or abet the suicide.
7. Prosecution evidence does not connect the applicants with the offence.
8. The applicants do not have any criminal history apart from this case.
9. The applicants are not flight risk.
The applicant being law abiding citizen have always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to cooperate with the court proceedings.
There is no possibility of their influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.

Let the applicants- Smt. Ramo Alias Ramrati and Rajesh be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicants will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
(ii) The applicants will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

Order Date :- 7.7.2023 "
8.

According to the learned counsel for applicant no such material has yet emerged on the basis of which it can be inferred that the deceased committed suicide on account of an immediate act of applicant or the applicant has even abetted, instigated or conspired in the commission of the alleged crime.
With reference to the material on record, he submits that the deceased was a short tempered lady and she has taken the extreme step of terminating her life by consuming some poisonous substance.
He also contends that there is no such distinguishing feature on the basis of which case of present applicant can be so distinguished from aforesaid bailed out co-accused so as to deny him bail.

He therefore submits that in view of above and for the facts and reasons recorded in the bail Abhishek Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 11 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71944099/
3 order dated 07.07.2023, applicant is also liable to be enlarged on bail on the ground of parity.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even otherwise applicant is a man of clean antecedents inasmuch he has no criminal history to his credit except the present one.
Applicant is in custody since 24.05.2023.
As such, he has under-gone more than two months of incarceration.

The police report (charge-sheet) in terms of Section 173 (2)
Cr.P.C. has already been submitted.
As such the entire evidence sought to be relied upon by the prosecution against applicant stands crystalized.
However, upto this stage, no such circumstance has emerged necessitating the custodial arrest of applicant during the pendency of trial.
He therefore contends that applicant is liable to be enlarged on bail.
In case the applicant is enlarged on bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall co-operate with the trial.
9. Per contra, the learned A.G.A. for state and the learned counsel for first informant have opposed the prayer for bail.
However, they could not dislodge the factual and legal submissions urged by learned counsel for applicant with reference to the record at this stage.

10. Having heard the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State, the learned counsel representing first informant, upon consideration of material on record, evidence, gravity and nature of offence, accusations made as well as complicity of applicant coupled with the fact that applicant is the devar of the deceased, the deceased has died on account of having committed suicide, no external ante-mortem injuries were found on the body of the deceased by the autopsy surgeon who conducted the autopsy on the body of the deceased, co-accused father-in-law and mother-in-law of the deceased have already been enlarged on bail by this Court, there is no such distinguishing feature on the basis of which, case of present applicant can be so distinguished from aforementioned co-accused so as to deny him bail, period of incarceration undergone, clean antecedents of applicant, the charge sheet having been submitted therefore entire evidence sought to be relied upon by the prosecution against applicant stands crystalized, learned A.G.A. and the learned counsel representing first informant could not point out any such circumstance necessitating the custodial arrest of applicant during the course of trial but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, applicant has made out a case for bail.
11. Accordingly the bail application is allowed.

12. Let the applicant-Abhishek Kumar involved in aforesaid case crime number be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) Applicant will not tamper with prosecution evidence.
(ii) Applicant will abide the orders of court, will attend the court on every date and will not delay the disposal of trial in any manner whatsoever.
(iii) Applicant will not indulge in any unlawful activities.
(iv) Applicant will not misuse the liberty of bail in any manner whatsoever.
